thread:
Sam: FYI we're onboarding a seeded customer (Vector Labs) and need accelerated capacity in eu-west-2 and ap-south-1. Request: 4x p5, 2x p4d, and burst g5 capacity for inference. Also will need ENI increases on the new accounts. Can infra help open the AWS quota requests?
Maya: Got it — which AWS account IDs and do they want regional isolation (separate accounts per region) or a single account?
Sam: Account IDs: 123456789012 (eu-west-2), 210987654321 (ap-south-1). They want a single customer account per region for compliance.
Andre: Important: p5/p4d in those regions require ENI and vCPU soft limits increased too. We'll likely need to request: "EC2 instance limit (accelerator)" for p5/p4d/g5, "Running On-Demand Standard (vCPUs)", and "Elastic Network Interfaces". Also confirm whether they need placement-group / cluster networking.
Sam: They will use spread placement across 2 AZs, not a strict placement group. Expected steady-state: 4 concurrent p5 serving nodes with burst to 8 during load tests.
Jin: Cost note — p5 is expensive on-demand. If Vector is ok with reserved or savings plan we can reduce cost but for now approvals should be for on-demand capacity. Back-of-envelope: p5 ~ $7.8/hr (us-east list) but eu-west-2 pricing ~ $9/hr. Include that in the internal ticket so finance signs off. :money_with_wings:
Maya: Copy. I'll open the AWS Support ticket — need the exact quota names and requested new limits. Sam can you paste the CLI snippet you used for other requests?
Sam: Sure — here's what I usually send (replace ACCOUNT_ID and REGION):
```
aws support create-case --region us-east-1 --service-code ec2 --category-code "instance-limits" --severity-code low --communication-body "Requesting increased accelerator instance quotas for ACCOUNT_ID in REGION: p5 -> 10, p4d -> 5, g5 -> 20. Also request ENI per subnet to 100 and On-Demand vCPU to 10,000 for accelerator usage. Use case: inference/production for Vector Labs (PII isolated), expected sustained throughput 4 nodes."
```
Andre: Also attach the AZ subnet IDs and VPC CIDRs. If subnets are small we'll hit ENI IP exhaustion quickly. Recommend upping per-subnet ENI and verifying ENI automatic allocation with the tenant's VPC team.
Sam: VPC CIDRs: 10.40.0.0/22 (eu-west-2), 10.80.0.0/22 (ap-south-1). Subnet sizes are /24. We should raise ENI per subnet to 50 and consider /23 if customer approves.
Maya: Opening ticket now. I'll include the provided CLI blob and ask for quota increases to be applied to both accounts and for default quota to be adjusted where possible.
infra-bot: Ticket created: AWS-20914. Assigned to Maya. ETA from AWS support typically 48-72h for accelerator requests.
Sam: Adding expected launch window: we want capacity available by 2026-04-08 for integration tests. Please tag as time-sensitive.
Andre: One more operational note — for p4d in eu-west-2 we need to pre-warm the instance-backed AMIs and ensure AMI has NVME driver + NCCL pinned libs. I'll prep an AMI build job.
Jin: For cost mitigation: consider mixed instance types behind autoscaler (p5 + g5) for batch loads. For latency-critical paths, keep p5 pinned.
Maya: AWS case updated with account IDs, requested numbers, VPC details, and time window. I've asked AWS to cc our billing contact: billing@vectorlabs.com.
Sam: Thanks. If AWS asks for business justification: state "production LLM inference for Vector Labs; regulated data; must pin dedicated GPU resources for SLA and data isolation".
Andre: I'll follow up on ENI increases and VPC subnet resizing after AWS confirms instance quotas.
Sam: Great — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Maya: Ping me if you want me to escalate to AWS TAM.
infra-bot: Update on AWS-20914: initial response received, AWS requested additional justification for vCPU limits.
Sam: I'll draft a justification doc and paste it here.
Andre: Marking as tracking: #onboard-vector.
Jin: Also, note AP-south-1 p5 availability is limited — if AWS declines, fallback plan is to deploy p5s in ap-southeast-2 and route traffic via closer edge nodes.
Sam: Noted. Will include fallback region in ticket. Thanks all.
